messages:
sasha: heads-up — NovaCorp asked for an org-level routing override so all their requests hit their dedicated pool. they want header-based pinning: X-Redwood-Org: novacorp + X-Redwood-Route: dedicated-novacorp-v1. can we approve?

riley: do we have telemetry+cost estimate if we pin an org to dedicated for a week vs indefinite? need SLO/cost implications.

kevin: agree we need numbers. also UX: console should capture reason, approver, TTL, and link to audit log. we should avoid free-form overrides in console. propose an "Enterprise Exceptions" flow w/ approval + auto-expire.

priya: security question — header-only overrides are spoofable. any plan to require a signed header or workspace-scope token? we should at least HMAC the header with a shared key or use a client cert.

amanda: +1 on signing. for onboarding we could accept header for testing, but prod must be either signed header or route via internal identity (org header validated by edge). also need a test mode flag so we can simulate.

kevin: proposal sketch: console flow creates an exception object: {org_id, route_id, approver, ttl_seconds, reason, enforcement_mode}. enforcement_mode = allowlist | signed-header | mTLS. default TTL 30d, max 365d with exec-level approve.

sasha: NovaCorp asked for 90d TTL. they want immediate start next deploy window. they're on an enterprise contract.

riley: from telemetry POV we need events: route_override.requested, route_override.approved, route_override.revoked, route_override.hit. attach tokenized cost projections and sample percent of traffic. dashboards should show active exceptions and per-org hit rate.

kevin: agree. add audit rows in infra logs and an admin UI that shows who created the override and the signed artifact. we must also add an alert when an override causes error rate or latency regression.

priya: corner case: what if an org header gets stripped by a proxy? we should document header precedence and fallback to org-id in JWT. also need a revocation API that customers can call to opt-out if misrouted.

amanda: won't blocking by denylist be easier? e.g., deny all non-dedicated pools for that org unless exception exists. less header logic in edge routing.

kevin: implementation note: route matcher currently accepts header predicates. we can add a higher-precedence exception table checked before normal routing. table entry: (org_id, route_id, enforcement_mode, expires_at).

sasha: can we ship a minimal safe path: (1) console form that creates exception in read-only mode (no enforcement) for 48h to test telemetry; (2) once verified, admin toggles enforcement to signed-header. helps avoid immediate blast radius.

riley: that sounds reasonable. I'll scope telemetry events and dashboard widgets. can we include cost delta = projected_tokens_in_override * per_token_delta? simple estimate first.

deploy-bot: created ticket ENG-3421: "Enterprise routing exceptions — NovaCorp request + exception flow" and linked to CI job pipeline.

kevin: assign to @kevin and @riley for initial RFC + POC. PR checklist: change in matcher precedence, exception table migration script, console form, audit logging, telemetry events.

priya: security will review the HMAC flow. I'll draft threat model notes.

amanda: i'll coordinate with customer success for the approval paperwork and confirm NovaCorp is ok with signed-header approach.

sasha: thanks everyone. next steps: kevin/riley to draft RFC by EOD Friday; priya to provide security constraints; amanda to confirm customer acceptance. I'll hold the customer until enforcement-ready. :thumbsup:
